pages.title: Community Evaluations and Evidence Accumulation
pages.text: Community Evaluations and Evidence Accumulation EEG analysis and behavioral modeling of implicit community evaluations and resident well-being. As a research assistant at Minzu University of China, supervised by Dr. Ze Geng, I completed all data analyses for this collaborative project on community environments and resident well-being. The study combines questionnaires, a community–valence Implicit Association Test (IAT), and EEG. I preprocessed the EEG recordings, extracted single-trial centroparietal positivity (CPP) slopes, and fit drift diffusion models to IAT response times and accuracy using PyDDM. I used BIC to compare models and incorporated CPP slopes into drift-rate models to examine the relationship between neural and behavioral evidence accumulation. The manuscript, “Community Environment and Resident Well-Being from an Affordance Perspective: Implicit Associations and Evidence Accumulation,” has been submitted to the Journal of Environmental Psychology . I am the second author; Ze Geng is the corresponding author.

pages.title: Human Factors in Driving Takeover
pages.text: Human Factors in Driving Takeover Cognitive load, warning timing, and situation-awareness recovery in automated driving. This independent project examines how cognitive load and the interval between monitoring and takeover requests relate to drivers’ situation-awareness recovery and takeover performance in a two-stage warning system. I independently developed a Unity-based VR driving scenario using PICO 4 Pro, integrating eye tracking with ECG, GSR, and EMG recording. The experimental design considers stable individual differences, including personality and driving style, alongside cognitive load and warning timing.

pages.title: Human Performance During Whole-Body Motion
pages.text: Human Performance During Whole-Body Motion Unity experiments and task-relative motion analysis on a 6-DOF platform. At the Institute of Software, Chinese Academy of Sciences, I developed a Unity-based directional-judgment task on a 6-DOF motion platform. The study included 39 participants and related response times to trial-level, task-relative components of platform acceleration: directional congruency and lateral interference. Reaction times showed no clear monotonic gradient across motion-intensity conditions. The two motion components showed opposite associations with response time in the pooled model, but neither association was clearly supported after adjustment for target direction. The manuscript, “Beyond Motion Intensity: Task-Relative Motion Geometry and Directional Response Time During Whole-Body Motion,” has been submitted to CHI 2027 . An earlier preprint is available under the title “Does Motion Intensity Impair Cognition in HCI? The Critical Role of Physical Motion-Visual Target Directional Congruency.”

pages.title: Human-AI Ethics
pages.text: Human-AI Ethics PsychoPy experiments and mixed-effects analysis of AI supervision and ethical decisions. This project investigates how AI supervision and incentive mechanisms influence dishonest behavior and ethical decision-making. I designed and programmed the behavioral experiments in PsychoPy and analyzed the data using Python/R and mixed-effects models. The resulting article was published in Acta Psychologica Sinica . Read the article .

pages.title: Behavioral Decision Modeling
pages.text: Behavioral Decision Modeling Drift diffusion and reinforcement-learning models for loss and compensatory decisions. During my research internship at Shenzhen University, supervised by Prof. Zhenhong He, I worked on loss and compensation in decision-making. I designed and programmed behavioral tasks in PsychoPy, developed Python data-analysis pipelines, and applied drift diffusion and reinforcement-learning models to behavioral data. This work connects experimental psychology with computational accounts of decision-making.

pages.title: EEG and ERP Analysis
pages.text: EEG and ERP Analysis Neural data analysis in studies of effort-based behavior and social relationships. As project leader in a study of effort-based behavior, I collected and analyzed behavioral and ERP data using Python/R. The experiment used a Monetary Incentive Delay task to examine input costs and reward/punishment cues. The related ERP manuscript has been submitted. In an earlier collaborative project on social networks and neural similarity, I preprocessed and analyzed EEG data using MATLAB and Python. These projects provided practical experience with neural data alongside behavioral measures.

pages.title: Jianshu Wang
pages.text: Jianshu Wang Human Factors | Cognitive Neuroscience | Behavioral Modeling Research Assistant, Minzu University of China B.S. in Applied Psychology, Henan University (2026) jishuu825@gmail.com I am a research assistant at Minzu University of China, supervised by Dr. Ze Geng, and a research intern at the Institute of Software, Chinese Academy of Sciences. I received my B.S. in Applied Psychology from Henan University in 2026. I study human cognition and behavior, with interests in how people interact with technology, one another, and their environments. My interests range from the cognitive and neural processes underlying behavior to the design of systems and environments that support human performance and well-being. pages.title: bookshelf
pages.text: bookshelf What an astonishing thing a book is. It’s a flat object made from a tree with flexible parts on which are imprinted lots of funny dark squiggles. But one glance at it and you’re inside the mind of another person, maybe somebody dead for thousands of years. Across the millennia, an author is speaking clearly and silently inside your head, directly to you. Writing is perhaps the greatest of human inventions, binding together people who never knew each other, citizens of distant epochs. Books break the shackles of time. A book is proof that humans are capable of working magic. – Carl Sagan, Cosmos, Part 11: The Persistence of Memory (1980) Books that I am reading, have read, or will read
